example_summary: Ankur received ₹ 5 lacs as rent from Yahoo Movies Ltd. for film shooting on his agricultural land in Kerala and claimed exemption u/s 10(1).
source_provision:
### **Statutory Framework: Agricultural Income & Exemption Test**

| Provision / Judicial Precedent | Core Statutory Condition | Legal Characterization | Tax Treatment / Head |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Section 10(1) r.w.s. 2(1A)(a)** | Rent/revenue derived from land situated in India & used for agricultural purposes | Exempt Agricultural Income | Fully Exempt u/s 10(1) |
| **CIT v. Raja Benoy Kumar Sahas Roy (SC)** | Must involve basic operations (tilling, sowing, planting) requiring human skill & labor | Core Agricultural Activity Benchmark | Qualifies for Sec 10(1) Exemption |
| **B. Nagi Reddi v. CIT (Mad HC)** | Commercial use (e.g., film shooting) on agricultural land without nexus to agricultural operations | Non-Agricultural Revenue | Taxable u/s 56 (IFOS) |


### **Statutory Conditions Checklist u/s 2(1A)**

* **Land & Location:** Land must be situated in India and actively used for agricultural purposes.
* **Direct Nexus Rule:** Income must be directly derived from agricultural operations, sale of agricultural produce, or qualifying farm building.


> [!WARNING] Judicial Benchmark on Use of Land: Mere ownership or physical presence of agricultural land is insufficient. If land is put to commercial use like film shooting, the revenue has no direct nexus with agricultural operations and fails the test of Section 2(1A).
